clue.text: Lack of interest in a course with happy ending

parts.note: a path is a route or course

indicators.note: the ending of the word happy is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone bored by a course of study that ends happily enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifference or listlessness, a lack of interest or concern, is the meaning of this noun.

clue.text: Current clerical office's fidelity

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a curacy is the office of a curate

explanation.surface: A present-day church post is a matter of faithfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelity can mean exactness or correctness, as in a faithful copy.

clue.text: A drink date where Henry met Constable

parts.note: gin is a drink
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A drinks date at which a man called Henry met a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry V met the French army led by the Constable of France, Charles d'Albret; 'Constable' is not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1415 battle between Henry V and the French force commanded by the Constable of France.

clue.text: Spring came, finally producing optimism

parts.note: to hop is to spring or jump

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of came

explanation.surface: Springtime arrived at last, bringing a sense of optimism.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopefulness, expecting good things, is a synonym of this noun.

clue.text: Vindictive English earl goes in very nearly drunk

indicators.note: goes in means the English earl letters are placed inside the other pieces
nearly means the last letter of the word for drunk is dropped

parts.note: full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A spiteful English aristocrat stumbles in, almost legless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as a description of the earl, but it supplies a synonym that 'nearly' shortens; 'goes in' places the English earl inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seeking revenge is vindictive; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Leave out a novel nonetheless for judge

indicators.note: novel means the letters are arranged in a new way

parts.note: none is O, nil, and less says it is taken away from the letters

explanation.surface: Still, skip a novel when you come to judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' splits as none (O) plus less: LEAVE OUT A without O is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge something is to assess or appraise it, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Data base covers outdated middle course

indicators.note: covers means the data word is wrapped round the outdated word

parts.note: gen is slang for information or data
old can mean outdated or no longer current
mean can mean base or low

explanation.surface: A database protects old-fashioned records.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the moderate path between two extremes, a middle course.

clue.text: Escape out of large box

indicators.note: out of means the large letter is taken from the word for escape

parts.note: flight is escape, as in taking flight

explanation.surface: Getting out of a big crate.
explanation.definitionFit: To box is to fight with the fists, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Ulster flounders reflected light

indicators.note: flounders means the word Ulster struggles about and is jumbled

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland struggles to shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounders' looks like fish but is the verb meaning stumbles about.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen or gloss, the light reflected from a surface, is a synonym of this noun.

clue.text: Old invader, possibly obtuse

definitions.meaning: a member of a Germanic people who invaded Britain in the fifth century
an obtuse one is a geometric example, between 90 and 180 degrees

explanation.surface: An ancient invader, perhaps rather slow-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles settled in England; geometrically, an obtuse one is an example of the shape between lines.

clue.text: Saintly old shoemaker's neat home

parts.note: crisp can mean neat and tidy
in means at home

explanation.surface: A description of a holy cobbler from the past and his tidy house.
explanation.walkthrough: St Crispin is the patron saint of shoemakers and cobblers.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Crispin, a third-century martyr, is traditionally said to have worked making shoes.

clue.text: Everyone tiptoes, ignoring Dutch claims

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: ignoring means the Dutch letter is left out of the verb

parts.note: to edge is to move cautiously, as one tiptoes

explanation.surface: Everybody creeps quietly about, paying no heed to the Dutch, and makes assertions.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, so the verbs mean the same.

clue.text: After my turns, knee's beginning to wobble

indicators.note: turns means the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: the beginning of knee's is its first letter

explanation.surface: After I spin round, my knee starts to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: COR, a British exclamation like 'my!', reversed by 'turns' gives ROC.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to sway or move unsteadily to and fro, which is to wobble.

clue.text: City recluse got shifted

indicators.note: shifted means the letters of recluse got are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A hermit was made to move to an urban place.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloucester is a cathedral city in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucester is an English cathedral city, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: In journal, son writes where to get drugs

indicators.note: In means the son and writing words sit inside the journal

parts.note: a diary is a journal
pens means writes

explanation.surface: A son records in his diary where he obtains drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy or clinic room dispensing medicines is where one obtains them.

clue.text: Piece about American person once removed?

indicators.note: about means the coin goes around the American letters

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money
US means American

explanation.surface: A news piece about an American who has been expelled once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once removed' is a genealogical term for a cousin one generation apart, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative described as once removed is typically a cousin of a different generation.

clue.text: Take cat first of all into school

indicators.note: into means the cat and letter go inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of the word all

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring the cat to school before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' is read literally: the first letter of 'all', A.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or take it, as in 'I can't take any more'.

clue.text: Dodge speech lacking constant shape

parts.note: a con is a dodge or trick

indicators.note: lacking means the constant letter is removed

parts.note: diction is manner of speech
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Avoiding talk that lacks a consistent form.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good shape means being in good condition; the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: First person to insult Orcadian perhaps

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun
to slander is to insult or defame

explanation.surface: Someone is the first to insult a person from Orkney.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orcadian is a native of Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Orkney lives on an island, so an Orcadian is an example.

clue.text: West, almost neglectful, uses sweet talk

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the neglectful word is cut

parts.note: heedless means careless or neglectful

explanation.surface: A Westerner, rather careless, uses flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone with flattery is to cajole them, the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: With difficulty, install bug in Austrian hotel

indicators.note: install means the bugging word is put inside the Austrian abbreviation

parts.note: Aus. is a dictionary abbreviation for Austria or Austrian
to tap a phone is to bug it
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A spy struggles to plant a listening device in a hotel in Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means only if necessary or with effort, so it suits doing something with difficulty.

clue.text: Pot, one wrapped in sock

indicators.note: wrapped in means the one letter sits inside the word for sock

parts.note: to sock someone is to punch them
a means one

explanation.surface: A cooking pot, with one item wrapped up in a sock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot or pot belly is a large protruding stomach, a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Most secure small 23 in disorder

indicators.note: in disorder means those letters are jumbled

parts.note: 23 refers to the answer of clue 23, a word for stunts

explanation.surface: The most secure small stunts are a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' points to the answer of 23 Down, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective meaning secure or protected.

clue.text: Stunts? Female scoffs

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A woman sneers at daredevil tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffs' looks like mocks but means eats greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunts are daring exploits or achievements, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Notice Bedford, say, initially takes forever to make profits

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a Bedford is a make of van

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of takes

parts.note: ages, as in 'it took ages', means a very long time

explanation.surface: A notice says a Bedford van takes forever to turn a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedford was a British brand of vans and lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: Benefits or gains can be called advantages, as in profiting from a situation.

clue.text: Watch old poet, forgetting king

indicators.note: forgetting means the king letter is omitted

parts.note: Virgil was the ancient Roman poet
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on an ancient poet who has forgotten a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A night watch, staying awake to keep guard or pray, is a synonym of this noun.

clue.text: Tours for one avoiding lake that's foul

indicators.note: avoiding means one lake letter is dropped from the French word

parts.note: Tours is a French town, ville in French

explanation.surface: A trip that keeps away from the lake is a nasty one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tours' looks like trips but is the French city; VILLE loses one L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vile is disgusting or foul; the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Wife lives on Henry's whim

parts.note: is means exists or lives
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A wife depends on Henry's passing fancies.
explanation.definitionFit: A desire or fancy can be called a whim; the nouns overlap in meaning.

clue.text: No good entering bovine team in white?

indicators.note: entering means the no good letters go inside the animal

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope of the bovine family

explanation.surface: A useless ox joins a side dressed in white.
explanation.walkthrough: England's national football and cricket teams traditionally play in white.
explanation.definitionFit: The English national side wears white shirts, so it is an example of a team in white.

clue.text: Hearing about four or six piddling

indicators.note: about means the trial goes around the numeral

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
four is IV in Roman numerals; six, VI, also works in a different place

explanation.surface: A court hearing over a sentence of four or six years seems petty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numeral for six, read the other way, sits one place later in the same word, so either number works.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is of little importance, the same as piddling or petty.

clue.text: Tip cart over where Henry suffered wounds

parts.note: to tilt is to tip

indicators.note: over means the cart word is turned round

parts.note: a dray is a heavy cart

explanation.surface: An instruction to overturn a cart where King Henry was hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII was badly injured in a jousting fall, at the tiltyard at Greenwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A jousting arena was where Henry VIII received his famous injuries.

clue.text: Stuff bathing suit, not all of it

indicators.note: not all of it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone crams a swimsuit, but not all of it fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff in the sense of possessions or items is a synonym for this plural noun.
